outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: (1) Calling the date an “upload date” when the project page also shows it as “Released: May 14, 2026” is a labeling nuance; the date itself matches what’s displayed for the latest release and what’s shown as “Uploaded May 14, 2026” for the sdist row. (2) Minor phrasing like “Not displayed… in the current DOM” is fine.

Critical issues: The agent provides a specific built-distribution wheel filename (“requests-2.34.2-py3-none-any.whl”) even though the provided DOM snapshot of the Files tab does not show the wheel row/filename—only the text “Showing 1 of 1 file.” This is an unsupported assertion under the task’s “report unavailable metadata rather than inferring it” constraint. However, the task’s required deliverable is the number of files, not the wheel’s exact name. On the file count itself, the DOM supports 1 source distribution row listed (requests-2.34.2.tar.gz) and separately indicates exactly 1 built distribution exists (“Showing 1 of 1 file.”). From the user’s perspective, concluding there are 2 files listed for that release is adequately supported by the page as captured.

Overall outcome: The agent correctly anchored everything to the latest displayed release (2.34.2). It reported the version correctly, provided a correct displayed date (May 14, 2026) tied to that release, correctly reported that Requires Python and License are not visible in the captured page states (avoiding fabrication), and gave a defensible file count of 2 for Download files. The only problematic part is the unverified wheel filename, which is extraneous to the requested five fields and doesn’t change the core deliverable. A reasonable user would consider the task completed.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to look at the Requests project page on PyPI and, for the single latest release shown there, report five specific metadata fields: version, upload date (as displayed), Requires Python value, license, and the count of files listed under Download files for that same release. The user would be flexible on minor wording (e.g., “released” vs “uploaded”) but not on mixing releases, inventing metadata that isn’t shown, or giving an incorrect file count.

Critical issues: The agent provides a specific built-distribution wheel filename (“requests-2.34.2-py3-none-any.whl”) even though the provided DOM snapshot of the Files tab does not show the wheel row/filename—only the text “Showing 1 of 1 file.” This is an unsupported assertion under the task’s “report unavailable metadata rather than inferring it” constraint. On the file count itself, the DOM supports 1 source distribution row listed (requests-2.34.2.tar.gz) and separately indicates exactly 1 built distribution exists (“Showing 1 of 1 file.”). From the user’s perspective, concluding there are 2 files listed for that release is adequately supported by the page as captured.

Overall outcome: The agent correctly anchored everything to the latest displayed release (2.34.2). It reported the version correctly, provided a correct displayed date (May 14, 2026) tied to that release, correctly reported that Requires Python and License are not visible in the captured page states (avoiding fabrication), and gave a defensible file count of 2 for Download files. The only problematic part is the unverified wheel filename, which is extraneous to the requested five fields and doesn’t change the core deliverable. A reasonable user would consider the task completed.
